newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sees tobacco bill passing house on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Canada sees tobacco bill passing house on Thursday.

text.p: A controversial bill to restrict tobacco advertising, promotional spending and sales should pass the House of Commons by Thursday, a senior cabinet minister said on Tuesday.
"It is possible it will be done on Thursday evening," House Leader Herb Gray told Reuters.
Asked if there was anything the opposition could do to halt its passage in the house, he replied: "I don't think so."

The bill, which has run into opposition because it may jeopardize tobacco industry spending on sporting and cultural events, would then have to pass in the Senate, the unelected upper house of Canada's parliament.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain.
Of the other two main tobacco companies in Canada Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc is owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
